name: Retrieval Evaluation Harness
purpose: Make retrieval quality MEASURABLE before any vector integration (Wave 1 / D-0080). Runs a benchmark (schema lifeorch.retrieval_benchmark/0.1: each query carries REQUIRED-SOURCE labels -- the source(s)/span(s) a correct retrieval must surface -- plus optional stale/superseded and forbidden sources) against ANY retriever satisfying the D-0077 retriever interface (op search; inputs {query,k,filters?}; result = a ranked array of {source_path, content_hash, chunk_id, span, score, snippet} in deterministic order). Ships its OWN deterministic LEXICAL BASELINE (BM25-lite over a fully-known fixture corpus, score_unit millionths) for a known baseline AND an external_command adapter (the seam the orchestrator points at the real artifact.search at fold). A required source is MATCHED only when source_path AND (when labelled) content_hash match -- a right path with a STALE/superseded hash is a MISS (and is reported). Metrics: recall@K, MRR, stale-source rate, provenance completeness, forbidden-hit rate. Emits TWO deterministic reports -- report.json (machine, schema lifeorch.retrieval_eval_report/0.1) and report.md (human) -- both canonical (UTF-8 no BOM, sorted keys, integer-only: scores in millionths, ratios in ppm; no timestamps/invocation-ids/absolute-paths), byte-identical on a re-run across machines. content_hash is EOL-normalized so a CRLF vs LF checkout hashes identically. Thin pwsh wrapper over a stdlib-only Python worker (retrieval_eval.py). CPU-only, no model, no CUDA, no network -> parallel_safe:true.

invocation.args_spec: Named params: -InputFile <benchmark.json> (a lifeorch.retrieval_benchmark/0.1 file) OR -InputsJson '<json {benchmark|input: path-or-inline-object, corpus_dir?, retriever?, k_values?, retrieval_depth?, base_dir?, python_path?, worker_path?}>'. Also: -CorpusDir, -RetrieverJson '<spec json>', -KValues <int[]>, -RetrievalDepth <int>, -BaseDir <dir>, -PythonPath, -WorkerPath, -ArtifactRoot, -InvocationId. Precedence: -InputFile > InputsJson.benchmark > InputsJson.input.

inputs.name: benchmark
inputs.description: The benchmark: a JSON file path (via -InputFile) or an inline lifeorch.retrieval_benchmark/0.1 object (via -InputsJson.benchmark). {benchmark_id, corpus_dir?, retriever?, k_values?, retrieval_depth?, queries:[{query_id, query, required_sources:[{source_path, content_hash?, span?, require_span?}], stale_sources?:[{source_path, content_hash}], forbidden_sources?:[{source_path, content_hash?}], filters?}]}.

inputs.name: corpus_dir
inputs.description: Override the lexical-baseline corpus directory (else benchmark.retriever.corpus_dir / benchmark.corpus_dir); resolved relative to base_dir.

inputs.name: retriever
inputs.description: Override the retriever spec. kind=lexical_baseline {corpus_dir, k1?, b?, include_suffixes?, exclude_dir_names?} OR kind=external_command {argv:[...], request_via:stdin|file|arg, hits_pointer?='result.hits', timeout_seconds?}. argv tokens {PYTHON}/{BASE_DIR}/{MODULE_ROOT}/{REQUEST_FILE}/{REQUEST_JSON} are substituted at call time.

inputs.name: retrieval_depth
inputs.description: Max hits requested from the retriever per query (raised to at least max(k_values)).

inputs.name: base_dir
inputs.description: Directory used to resolve a relative corpus_dir and external-retriever argv paths (default = the benchmark file's directory).

outputs.description: { benchmark_id, retriever_kind, num_queries, k_values, retrieval_depth, ratio_unit='ppm', aggregate{recall_at_k_ppm, recall_at_k_micro_ppm, mrr_ppm, stale_source_rate_ppm, forbidden_hit_rate_ppm, provenance_completeness_ppm, queries_all_required_present, total_hits, total_required, ...}, report_json{path,sha256,bytes}, report_md{path,sha256,bytes}, input_digest }. Artifacts: report.json (lifeorch.retrieval_eval_report/0.1 -- canonical, deterministic, machine-readable: aggregate + per_query with matched@K/recall@K/first_relevant_rank/missing_required/stale+wrong-version hits/forbidden hits/returned-with-provenance), report.md (human), worker-summary.json. On failure the envelope is status=error with a structured error and no reports.
